activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Volumes of Solids Using Triple Integrals

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/770cdf03e988f811ccc3ff805889cef55304b01b6e8009e25ba128fbdbb89066.png)

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/8e5f3095cac4e068e54d9b3ac2bb55dc4789e7ca68d4524dce4d25a55abd5be6.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 4-2x-4z},
$$

where $D$ is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane.

To find the top boundary curve of $D$ in the form $z=z(x),$ we substitute $y=0$  into the equation $y=4-2x-4z:$

$$
0=4-2x-4z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{x}{2}
$$

Then, we have

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{2}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/76fcca4251a904a08ac2f6ba8181d92c2c2fa7e07e596ef6276f1d21b574817a.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{2},\,\,0\le y\le 4-2x-4z}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/2}{\int }_{0}^{4-2x-4z}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=4-2x-4z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/2}(4-2x-4z)-0\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/2}4-2x-4z\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(4-2x)z-2{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1-x/2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((4-2x)(1-\frac{x}{2})-2{(1-\frac{x}{2})}^{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(1-\frac{x}{2})((4-2x)-2(1-\frac{x}{2}))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(2-x)(2-x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2-2x+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,dx \\  & ={[2x-{x}^{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(2(2)-{2}^{2}+\frac{{2}^{3}}{6})-0 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
